description:
FILED s543j (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22) while fixing #5210 (`local %ENV`: the same shape).  PRE-EXISTING.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s543j/probes/file in the s543j worktree (agent-abcd8b98eb856dbee)/t5333.pl):
    $SIG{USR1} = 'IGNORE'; { local %SIG = (USR1 => sub { print "1 handled\n" }); kill 'USR1', $$; select(undef, undef, undef, 0.2); } print "2 after\n";
  perl: 1 handled / 2 after      PCL: 2 after
  (with no IGNORE before: `{ local %SIG; $SIG{USR1} = sub {...}; kill 'USR1', $$ }` -- PCL is KILLED by the signal, rc 138, probes/m4/d14 in the s543j worktree.)

MECHANISM: `local %SIG` lowers to a `let` of %SIG to a fresh table; %SIG's slots are magic cells (%p-signal-cell-box-p) that install the handler.  NOT the p-local-env macro (the env layer is a different store): a localizer of its own that saves every signal's disposition, empties them, fills through the %SIG store, and restores the dispositions on exit.  `local $SIG{K}` is right (the element macros keep the cell).

=== DONE (s543l) ===
Measured perl 5.40.3 first: `local %SIG` gives an EMPTY hash (keys 0, reads undef) but does NOT change a handler -- an
IGNOREd signal stays ignored, an outer sub handler still runs on delivery, an outer __WARN__ / __DIE__ still fires;
a store in the scope installs; at the exit every signal is back to the caller's (DEFAULT -> the next kill kills).
Fix: p-local-store :sig (see #5332): the scope's %SIG is a COPY of the caller's view -- the same stateless signal cells
(they read and write *p-sig-stored*, so a store installs at once), the other keys' values in fresh entries -- then the
list stored through it; the exit puts the view back and re-applies every signal whose stored value changed
(%p-sig-local-save / -fill / -restore).  The one difference left (docs/not-supported.md "%SIG"): a key the scope did
not store READS the caller's value where perl's empty hash reads undef (and `keys %SIG` counts them).  Probes m4
s01-s11: base 6 -> tree 10 = perl; s11 (`exists $SIG{X}` after `delete` inside the scope) is the documented ns-sig
item (it read N on the base only because the plain table dropped the cell).  The siblings: `local %ENV`, `local
@ARGV`, `local %+`, `local %main::` = perl on base and tree (nothing to file).  Guard signals-01.t 'local-sig' (row 3).
Filed #5380 (SILENT WRONG, pre-existing: a die in a handler of a signal SBCL runs DIRECTLY -- HUP INT TERM ALRM WINCH
by self-kill -- is lost; found while writing the guard, which uses USR1 for its dying handler).


=== s543l REVIEW FIX L1 (2026-11-27, Opus 5.5; WIP 9 eff8c239, stacked on s543m 9a11d52e) ===
The reviewing session found the batch's first form a regression of the VIEW: the scope's %SIG was a COPY of the caller's (67 keys, the caller's values; base = perl there: `{ local %SIG; keys %SIG }` 0, `defined $SIG{USR1}` false).  Now the scope's view is perl's EMPTY hash and the handlers stay the caller's until a store: the callers' views wait in *p-sig-outer-views*; a delivery (%p-sig-current-value) and the __WARN__ / __DIE__ hooks read %p-sig-entry (the current view's entry, else the innermost caller view's); a store to an absent signal key of the scope's view makes its signal cell first (%p-sig-view-cell: the element store's absent arm, the lvalue cell, `local $SIG{K}` through %p-lhe-slot), so it installs; a `local $SIG{K}` that made the key removes it at its exit and leaves the signal at its DEFAULT until the scope ends (perl's delete magic, probed); `delete` in the scope removes the key.  Measured readers (scratch/s543l/probes/m4b, 15 shapes perl -> base 9a11d52e -> tree): element read / exists / defined / keys / values / each / list / boolean / a copy / a slice / a store then keys / the hooks / nested / a sub twice / die out / alarm: base 11 -> tree 15 of 15 on stdout (v09's stderr = the USR2 runtime-owned announce); m4 24 of 24 (was 23: delete-then-exists in the scope).  Guard signals-01.t local-sig-view (row 4): fails on the first form (the view lines) and on the base (the handler lines).  Cost: one special-variable test on a hash store's ABSENT-key path and in %p-lhe-save / -init (measured in the batch's timing leg).


FINAL SHA (s543l, 2026-11-27): the batch is MERGE-READY at 2f85209e, rebased onto main 4b0d5d50 (its code = s543m final 5d426786 + this batch; the review fix L1 for #5333 is 6a1301ed); the notes above cite pre-rebase shas.
